motivation: more viewpoints and two capture radii should improve triangulation, and version1 (shot from across the lake) sees the roof, which version2 -- shot upward from the balustrade -- never does
method: COLMAP, 352 images, exhaustive matching (sequential cannot link two separate captures: it only compares neighbours in filename order)

headline_result.note: these numbers look healthy and are misleading

evidence.test: a walk photographed in order should have consecutive cameras close together; ratio of largest to median inter-camera step, scale-invariant
evidence.interpretation: the same 146 version2 photographs form a clean ring alone and a badly broken path inside the combined model, so the combination corrupted the geometry rather than the input being at fault

cause: four-fold rotational symmetry. Exhaustive matching compares every pair, so faces roughly 90 degrees apart -- nearly identical on a four-porched pavilion -- match each other. The mapper resolves those false correspondences into a self-consistent but globally wrong reconstruction, which is why the reprojection error stays sub-pixel.
significance: src/match_features.py restricts matching to adjacent frames for exactly this reason, documented for optical flow. This is the same failure reproduced in structure-from-motion, an independent algorithm.
decision: reconstruct from salathai_version2 alone (146/146 registered, 0.58px, verified clean ring). Fusing the two captures would need matching that cannot pair distant faces -- e.g. sequential within each capture plus vocabulary-tree loop closure with geometric verification -- not exhaustive.
cost: about 90 minutes: 60 matching, 27 mapping, on CPU

second_attempt.method: sequential matching within each walk plus vocabulary-tree loop detection, to propose only a bounded number of cross-capture candidates per image instead of every pair
second_attempt.reason: COLMAP 4.1.1 reads FAISS vocabulary indexes; the only published tree (demuc.de vocab_tree_flickr100K_words32K.bin) is the legacy FLANN format and aborts on load. No FAISS-format tree is published, and training one on this project's own 352 images would be degenerate -- vocabulary trees are meant to be learned from large, diverse collections.

final_decision: Reconstruct from salathai_version2 alone. Fusing the two captures is blocked by the subject itself rather than by tooling: any matching that proposes non-adjacent pairs can match one of the four near-identical faces to another, and exhaustive matching demonstrated that geometric verification does not reliably reject those. The captures also differ in illumination (version1 sunny, version2 overcast) and in distance, so even correct geometry would likely bake patchy appearance into a splatting model. The honest route to better coverage is a new capture designed for reconstruction -- varied heights, consistent lighting -- not forcing these two together.
